summary: Feed s142_double is degraded: NDR port severely overloaded by microbursts (29.95 Gbps on 10 Gbps port, 299% capacity) and encrypted traffic share 94.3% exceeds NDR tolerance of 90%, reducing payload inspection and causing burst drops.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker aggregates multiple high-rate sources onto a single 10 Gbps NDR port without load balancing or burst buffering. 1ms microburst peaked at 29.95 Gbps (299% of port capacity), indicating lack of distribution across tool ports.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR will drop packets during bursts, leading to incomplete flow reassembly, missed detections, and gaps in NDR coverage. Needs both directions and full payload but cannot keep up.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 3x10G tool ports with flow-aware hashing to keep per-port peaks below 80% and absorb microbursts without drops

findings.root_cause: 94.3% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC), above the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is forwarded encrypted with no prior decryption, leaving almost no cleartext payload for inspection.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires full payload for detection but can only use metadata (JA3, flow sizes, timing). Payload-based threat detection, C2 and exfiltration detection is severely limited.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS at the broker or forward session keys to the NDR to bring encrypted share below 90% and restore payload visibility for detection
